## Why

#135 brings the #132 spike's `TurnTrace` to `main`, so each coordinator turn is traced in Phoenix. `TurnTrace` only knows about the coordinator. Once workers exist (#60, #61, #64), a turn will also hold the workers' model calls and tool calls, often several workers at once (technical spec section 1). `TurnTrace` assumes every message from the SDK is the coordinator's, so it may mix a worker's model calls and tokens into the coordinator's spans. This spike finds a way to trace workers on the spike branch first, so `TurnTrace` has the right shape before it's on `main` with tests.

A **worker** is a subagent the coordinator starts with its `Agent` tool (technical spec section 6). A **trace** is the record of one turn, made of **spans**: one for the turn, and under it, in order, one for each model call and one for each tool call (research doc section 2.2).

## Design

- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), sections 2.2 (spans from our own code) and 3 ("Workers aren't traced yet"). The code is `src/agent/turn-trace.ts` on the [`spike/phoenix-evals`](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/tree/spike/phoenix-evals) branch.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 1 (the agents, and that workers run in parallel) and 6 (workers).
- The Agent SDK's types for 0.3.301, in `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts`. Start from these: the `agents` option and `AgentDefinition`, `parent_tool_use_id` on the SDK's messages and stream events, the `forwardSubagentText` option, and `getSubagentMessages()`. By default, the SDK sends only a worker's tool calls and tool results, not its text or thinking.

## Open questions

- How are a worker's turns traced in Phoenix? The Do items below answer it. Moved from #60 on 2026-10-25, where it was raised for the stay researcher.

## Do

Joe isn't available while this runs, so don't stop to wait for answers. When a choice comes up, make it, and list it in the PR's decisions comment. When something can't be made to work, write down what was tried and what failed, then go on to the next item.

Do the work on `spike/phoenix-evals`, with Phoenix running locally as in the #132 spike (`docker compose --profile evals up -d phoenix`). The server's Phoenix comes later, in #135. The code doesn't need to pass `npm run check`. That branch never gets a PR, so its code never reaches `main`. Push the code there, and make the research doc change on its own branch off `main`, for the PR.

- **Add a throwaway worker** on the spike branch, since no real one exists yet. Pass it to the coordinator in the SDK's `agents` option, and add `Agent` to the coordinator's allowed tools. Give the worker one tool from an MCP server the app already has, such as `find_place`, and a short instruction, such as "find two coffee shops near the place you're given." Put it on a different model from the coordinator's, such as `claude-sonnet-5-5`, so its model calls are easy to tell apart. Find a message for `npm run chat` that makes the coordinator start it, and one that starts two at once. The coordinator's instructions name no worker, so it may not call one from a message alone. If it doesn't, add a line about the worker to its instructions on the spike branch.
- **Find out what the SDK sends from a worker,** with `includePartialMessages` on as `TurnTrace` has it, and with `forwardSubagentText` off and on. For each, say whether these come through, and how each is tied to the worker: its thinking, its text, its tool calls with their inputs and results, and each of its model calls' token counts. Say whether the turn's result message counts the worker's tokens in its usage. If a worker's thinking or tokens can't be had from the stream, try `getSubagentMessages()`, and say what it gives and when it can be read.
- **Make `TurnTrace` trace workers.** Each worker gets its own span under the coordinator's `Agent` tool span, with its model call spans and tool spans under that, in order. Show it working with two workers at once, with neither one's spans under the other's. Check in Phoenix that the coordinator's own model call spans hold only the coordinator's tokens, and that the trace's and the session's token totals include the workers'.
- **Write the answers into `research/agent-evaluations.md`,** as a new section under Results, with the output that shows each one, such as a span tree like section 2.2's. Change section 3's bullet "Workers aren't traced yet" to say what was found, and what `TurnTrace` needs on `main`.

## Done when

- `research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it.
- On the spike branch, a chat turn that starts two workers shows up in Phoenix with each worker's spans under its own `Agent` tool span.

## Ends in

A PR with the research doc.

## Settled in

The PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
